sam_infra: FYI rolling CUDA 12 base images to eu-west-gpu pool triggered a small storm. seeing lots of short-lived OOMs and a few segfaults in our tiny repro kernels after the container rebuilds.

maya_sre: Ugh. Which image tag did we push?

sam_infra: rwinference/cuda-app:2026-11-cuda12-gcc13 (rebuild to pick up security fixes)

devon_runtime: Any driver mismatch logs? driver on nodes is 525.105 but CUDA12 expected 535+ iirc.

sam_infra: Ran a quick check: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv` shows 525.105 on most eu-west nodes. some AU nodes already bumped to 535.

ana_prod: Confirmed. Pods on nodes with 525 show `Illegal instruction (core dumped)` inside libcusparse ops. On 535 nodes they run fine.

maya_sre: That explains it — CUDA 12 builds linked against newer libcuda ABI. gcc13 + cuda12 toolchain produced binaries that assume newer driver symbols.

devon_runtime: We also saw a warning in the pod logs: `NCCL WARN NET/IB : ibv_fork_init() failed (err No such file or directory)` but the fatal is `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` then segfaults. Repro snippet: 
```
E tensorflow: F external/..../kernel.cu:123 assertion failed: 0
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
Aborted (core dumped)
```

sam_infra: Node kernel messages show `nvidia: module version 535.86 does not match kernel taint` on some upgraded nodes — messy state from partial driver upgrades.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4573 (labels: cuda12-rebuild). autoscaler paused on affected pools.

maya_sre: Immediate mitigation: 1) stop further canary pushes of cuda12 image, 2) roll back image tag for affected deployments to :2026-10-cuda11.8-gcc11, 3) cordon/evict only nodes with mixed driver state.

devon_runtime: Agree. Also start a targeted test matrix: image(tag) x driver(version) x kernel(version). We need to capture `modinfo nvidia`, `uname -r`, `ldconfig -p | grep cuda` from failing nodes.

sam_infra: I'll run a script to collect that and attach to the incident. quick grep output: `libnvidia-ml.so.1 => not found` on some containers — looks like the container runtime stripped vendor libs during rebuild. That may be a packaging change in our buildpacks with gcc13.

ana_prod: Cost/ops note: if we rollback to older images we might spike egress for around ~3TB as windows of traffic rehydrate caches. also dev tenants in us-west will be affected for ~30 mins during drain.

maya_sre: Can we instead pin the driver on nodes to 535 quickly? riskier but fewer app-level rollbacks. What's node churn impact?

sam_infra: Node driver upgrade requires reboot/taint cycle. eu-west pool has 120 GPUs; upgrading 535 across them will cause ~10-12% temporary capacity loss while reboots happen due to drain sequencing. With current load it's borderline but manageable if we do rolling upgrade overnight.

devon_runtime: For short term, rollback images + restart pods on stable nodes. For medium term, schedule driver bump+kernel recompile on a maintenance window and add preflight tests to our build pipeline that run small CUDA smoke tests against driver matrix.

maya_sre: Also add an automated check in the image build that fails if binaries reference a higher `GLIBCXX_3.4.30` or `CXXABI_1.4.0` than our runtime. We missed C++ ABI checks with gcc13.

sam_infra: Repro steps for infra team:
1) kubectl -n ml get pods -o wide | grep CrashLoop
2) ssh node && sudo journalctl -k -u nvidia-driver.service | tail -n 200
3) collect `/usr/bin/ldd /opt/release/bin/repro` and `strings /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcudart.so | grep CUDAABI`

devon_runtime: I'm going to prepare a small canary job matrix and a Github PR to add toolchain ABI gating. tagging @maya_sre for the incident plan.

maya_sre: Thanks. I'll coordinate the rollback and schedule the driver window for Tue 02:00 UTC. infra-bot, keep autoscaler paused until we confirm stable. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Autoscaler resumed for non-affected pools. Affected pools remain paused.

sam_infra: Will follow up with postmortem once we have artifacts. TL;DR: container rebuild with gcc13 + CUDA12 produced binaries that depend on newer driver/kernel symbols; mixed-driver fleet caused reproducible app crashes. Next: gate builds + plan driver rollouts.

ana_prod: Noted. please add an estimate of customer impact to INC-2026-4573.

sam_infra: Added note: ~4% of inference traffic in eu-west experienced retries; no data exposure.

devon_runtime: Pushing the PR now with ABI checks and a small smoke test.

maya_sre: Good work team. keep updates in thread.
